t: Look up at the walls and you may spot a plaster nose sticking out where no nose should be. These are the London Noses, sometimes called the Seven Noses of Soho. They're casts in plaster of Paris of the artist's own nose, made by Rick Buckley in 1997. Initially about thirty-five were fixed to buildings, including the National Gallery and Tate Britain. By 2011 only about ten survived, so each one you find is a bit of a survivor. They poke out in an unexpected way, and that's the joke.
